$comment: Aurelia Browser - Chromium pin configuration (single source of truth).
Never edit the revision fields by hand after a release: the update bot proposes
a change to this file, and a maintainer merges it after the patch set has been
Do not replace `revision` with a moving ref such as `main` or `latest`.

chromium.pinRationale: Current stable-channel build on Windows x64 - the first target platform - as published by chromiumdash, so the baseline is a promoted, security-patched release instead of an unpromoted branch head.
pinEvidence: gh api repos/chromium/chromium/contents/chrome/VERSION?ref=cfaadc5a132d78e1828635aa8405a499f3e14864 -> MAJOR=155 MINOR=0 BUILD=8059 PATCH=40
git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/chromium/chromium.git refs/tags/155.0.8059.40 -> cfaadc5a132d78e1828635aa8405a499f3e14864 (the GitHub mirror does expose release tags; verified 2026-10-07)
chromium.upstreamRefNote: The github.com/chromium/chromium mirror exposes release tags (refs/tags/<version>), and refs/tags/155.0.8059.40 resolves to the pinned commit cfaadc5a132d78e1828635aa8405a499f3e14864. It has no GitHub Releases objects, so the tags - not releases - are the mirror's usable marker. Chromium's own release branches are published on chromium.googlesource.com as refs/branch-heads/8059. The revision is recorded explicitly (never as a moving ref) and is additionally verified by reading chrome/VERSION at that revision and by matching pre-image digests.

pinHistory.note: Initial scaffolding pin. The revision is a real, tagged release-branch build (refs/tags/155.0.8059.73), but it sits later on branch-heads/8059 than the build chromiumdash reported as stable for the first target platform - it is an unpromoted PGO profile roll, not a promoted stable release, so it was the wrong baseline. Re-pinned to 155.0.8059.40; this entry is kept so the correction is auditable. An earlier note in this field claimed the mirror exposes no tags at all; that was wrong and was corrected after checking refs/tags directly.

rules: Never merge a Chromium update directly into main.

Detect -> open an issue with a candidate revision and the patch verification report -> dispatch the GitHub-hosted Chromium validation workflow -> run a separate runtime smoke test -> maintainer merge.
Security releases are prioritised but still verified before merge.
A pin change requires a matching `git apply` verification against the new revision.

depotTools.why: depot_tools has no GitHub mirror, so the revision was read from the canonical gitiles endpoint and pinned like any other source dependency. Update it deliberately, together with Chromium pin updates, and use the manual GitHub-hosted validation workflow to prove the combination works.

referenceBuilder.notes: Measured requirements are recorded once real builds run; see docs/BUILDING-CHROMIUM.md.

gnValidation.notes: Applies ONLY to validation_level=gn, which runs GN generation and gn check and never compiles. targeted and full keep the 150 GB referenceBuilder floor. RAM is 15.5 GB, not 16, because the OS-reported total on a nominal 16 GB machine can be slightly below 16. The GN disk floor of 80 GB is derived from evidence: depot_tools (~0.3 GB) + gclient sync --no-history shallow checkout of Chromium and its DEPS (~15-25 GB working tree + ~3-5 GB shallow .git for ~750 dependency repos at pinned SHA, per upstream fetch --no-history documentation and cl-shrink measurements of dependency .git overhead) + GN generation artifacts (~1-2 GB) + a 10 GB safety reserve that the run aborts before consuming. A 10 GB safety reserve is enforced during execution (independent of the pre-sync floor). Measured values are recorded per run in runner-capabilities.json.

targetedLite.notes: EXPERIMENTAL targeted-lite profile (M1.9, resource-aware targeted compilation). Applies ONLY to validation_level=targeted-lite: WebUI TypeScript/GRIT/pak resource compilation plus the two Aurelia C++ controller translation units (object-level MSVC compile). This is a SEPARATE profile and does not lower the targeted/full referenceBuilder gate (8 cores / 32 GB / 150 GB), which is unchanged. CPU and RAM match the measured standard windows-2025 runner (4 vCPU / 16 GB; RAM is 15.5 rather than 16 because the OS-reported total on a nominal 16 GB machine can be slightly below 16). The 80 GB pre-sync disk floor reuses the GN-only evidence base (run 38130837908 measured ~29.5 GB shallow sync + ~1.8 GB GN generation = ~31.3 GB) plus headroom for bounded compile outputs: the mode runs script-based WebUI resource actions and two controller translation units, with no dependency-library build, no link step and no chrome target. A 15 GB runtime disk reserve (compilation reserve) and the 1.5 GB memory reserve are enforced during execution and the process tree is stopped before the reserve is consumed. Measured values are recorded per run in runner-capabilities.json and resource-usage.jsonl.

buildRequirements.sandboxNote: The development sandbox used for scaffolding has ~20 GB free disk and cannot hold or build a Chromium checkout. Only lightweight upstream file verification runs there.
